summary: Esho Yamaguchi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University. He served as a professor at Osaka University from around 1968 to 1982, and held a post at Ritsumeikan University around 1982.
Eshun Otsuka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student (kenkyūsei) at Taisho University and also held a research student post there, attested in 2013.

Estela Piccin works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at the State University of Campinas, Associação Buddha-Dharma, Methodist University of São Paulo, and the Buddha-Dharma Centre of Hong Kong, later holding teaching and art director positions in Campinas.

Ester Bianchi is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Jean-Noël Robert and Alfredo Cadonna, earning degrees from Ca' Foscari University and EPHE. Her posts include Ca' Foscari, Florence, Perugia, and UC Berkeley.
Ethan Kroll is an Indology scholar who served as an editorial board member for Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies and held a post at Baker McKenzie, both attested in 2012.
Etienne Vermeersch was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from around 1953 to 1958. He later held an academic post at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997.

Etsuaki Teraishi is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, attested in 1999, and as a JSPS special research fellow, attested in 2001.

Indologist Eugen Hultzsch studied at Leipzig, Bonn, and under Georg Bühler. He worked as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of Madras and India (1886–1903) and served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied at Polytechnikum Riga and Riga Technical University. From 1881 to 1889, he served as Professor of National Economy and Lecturer of Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.

Eugen Prym specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University, the University of Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, and the University of Bonn under Johann Gildemeister, where he became Privatdozent of Oriental Languages in 1870.

Eugen Rose was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his studies at the University of Königsberg in 1929, the University of Bonn (Ph.D. 1929–1933), and the University of Marburg (dr. theol. 1929–1941).

Eugen Wilhelm was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Jena, where he earned his Ph.D. under August Schleicher. He later served as professor at the University of Jena.

Eugene N. Lane was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Princeton University and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Virginia from around 1962 to 1966 and the University of Missouri from around 1966 to 2000.

Eugene Watson Burlingame studied Indology and Buddhist studies at Yale, Penn, Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held fellowships at Penn and Johns Hopkins, and served as Lecturer in Pāli at Yale (1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and art history who studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield. He taught at the University of Chicago before becoming Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard University.

Eugeni d'Ors was a philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona from around 1897 to 1903 and at Universidad Central between 1912 and 1913. He later held an academic post at Universidad Central.

Eugenia Vanina is an Indologist and historian who earned her Ph.D. at Moscow State University between 1975 and 1981. In 1985, she took up a post as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Eugenio Frola was an Indologist and mathematician who studied engineering and mathematics at the Polytechnic University and University of Turin. He served as assistant and professor of mathematics at the Polytechnic University of Turin from around 1930 to 1962.

Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from around 1932 to 1941. He subsequently served as a professor at Leiden University from 1950 to 1983, succeeding C. C. Berg.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Jagiellonian University, Lviv under Andrzej Gawroński, and in Paris. He held academic posts at the University of Lviv, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, and the University of Warsaw.
